Present petition is directed against order dated 27.10.2023 passed by learned Additional Sessions Judge, Sonipat (Annexure P-11) in FIR No.684 dated 18.09.2023 registered under Sections 420/406/506 IPC at Police Station Kundli, Sonipat granting pre-arrest bail to respondent No.1- Sanjay Goyal @ Sanjay Kumar.
2 Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that it is a case wherein respondent No.1 in connivance with the other co-accused forged invoices.
However, the same has not been taken into consideration by the Court below while considering prayer of respondent No.1 for pre-arrest bail.

It has been further contended that the present occurrence has caused hardship to the present petitioner who has not been able to meet his financial liabilities arising out of the loan that he procured for purchasing these articles, which have been illegally usurped by the accused(s) including CRM-M No.63012 of 2023 (O&M) 22: 2023:PHHC: 161778 respondent No.1.
He further submits that respondent No.1 has not joined the investigation till date and is openly tampering with the evidence in possession of the investigating agency.

3 Having heard learned counsel for the petitioner and after going through records of the case, this Court finds that so far as the plea raised by the petitioner with respect to non-consideration of forgery at the hands of respondent No.1 is concerned, the same is misconceived.

Para 7 of the impugned order reads as under :-
"7.
The complainant has argued that said Bhavesh has no concern with M/s Balaji Overseas Exim, and one Krishan is a proprietor of M/s Balaji Overseas Exim.
He contended that invoice prepared by the applicant is forged.

However, the applicant has placed on record the screenshots of Chat between him and Bhavesh and it is Bhavesh, who had supplied the particulars of M/s Balaji Overseas Exim, to the M/S Kapalin Food Pvt. Ltd vs Sanjay Goyal And Anr on 16 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84052864/

sentences.text: 1 applicant for deposit of the amount of invoices in the account of M/s Balaji Overseas Exim.
Thus the applicant had already made the payment of the material purchased by him against invoice and he had also deposited the GST and filed GST return."
4 Thus, it cannot be said that the Court was not alive to the alleged forgery.
The court has recorded the contention raised by the present petitioner through his counsel before the Court and has also dealt with the same.

So far as the plea with respect to respondent No.1 violating any of the conditions as enumerated under Section 438(2) of the Code is concemed, the petitioner is required to move an appropriate application before the concerned Court seeking cancellation of bail, instead of availing remedy under Section 482 Cr.P.C.
CRM-M No.63012 of 2023 (O&M) 332: 2023:PHHC: 161778 5 Likewise, the financial constraints being faced by the petitioner cannot be a ground to interfere while exercising jurisdiction under Section 482 Cr.P.C. to cancel the bail which has been granted by the Court below by well reasoned order.
6 In view of above, the present petition is dismissed.
( PANKAJ JAIN )
JUDGE 16.12.2023 Pooja sharma-I Whether speaking/reasoned Yes Whether Reportable : No M/S Kapalin Food Pvt. Ltd vs Sanjay Goyal And Anr on 16 December, 2023
